FINAL NEXT STEP — BUILD THE IN-APP OWNER AUTHORIZATION BUTTON NOW

The root cause is confirmed.

The backend code is not the current blocker.

The remaining blocker is that the autonomous authorization endpoint is still receiving a stale or static Supabase token instead of the owner’s current live in-app session.

Proceed now.

Do not ask the owner to copy or paste any access token into chat.

Do not use IVX_OWNER_TOKEN_SESSION as the permanent solution.

==================================================
1. ADD THE OWNER BUTTON
==================================================

Add this button inside the existing authenticated IVX Owner Settings, Admin Hub, or IVX IA Owner Dashboard:

AUTHORIZE AUTONOMOUS QA

The button must only be visible to the registered IVX owner.

Use the current Supabase session automatically:

const {
  data: { session },
  error
} = await supabase.auth.getSession();

If no valid session exists:

1. Attempt one:
   supabase.auth.refreshSession()

2. If refresh fails:
   Redirect to the normal owner login.

3. After successful owner login:
   Retry the authorization request once.

Do not create infinite retries.

==================================================
2. CALL THE LIVE OWNER AUTHORIZATION ENDPOINT
==================================================

Call:

POST /api/ivx/senior-developer/generate-worker-access

Use:

Authorization: Bearer <session.access_token>

Request body:

{
  "action": "qa-production-verification",
  "commitSha": "<current GitHub main SHA>",
  "workerId": "ivx-senior-dev-01",
  "expiresInMinutes": 10
}

The access token must:

- Come directly from the current owner session
- Travel only through HTTPS
- Never appear in logs
- Never appear in the UI
- Never be stored in Render
- Never be stored in the database
- Never be sent into Rork chat

==================================================
3. VERIFY OWNER IDENTITY
==================================================

The backend must:

1. Call Supabase auth.getUser(accessToken).
2. Verify the returned user exists.
3. Verify auth user ID matches the registered production owner.
4. Verify owner email or owner record if required.
5. Reject non-owner users with HTTP 403.
6. Reject expired or invalid sessions with HTTP 401.

Expected:

- Valid owner session: HTTP 201
- Missing session: HTTP 401
- Expired session: HTTP 401
- Non-owner session: HTTP 403

Do not bypass the owner guard.

==================================================
4. GENERATE SHORT-LIVED WORKER ACCESS
==================================================

After owner validation:

- Generate a cryptographically secure random token.
- Bind it to:
  - exact action
  - exact commit SHA
  - exact worker ID
  - owner ID
  - expiration time
- Store only the SHA-256 hash.
- Return or forward the raw token only once.
- Write issuance to the proof ledger.

Required expiration:

5–15 minutes

Required use:

Single-use only

==================================================
5. HAND OFF DIRECTLY TO THE WORKER
==================================================

Prefer secure direct backend-to-worker handoff.

Do not expose the raw worker token in the user interface unless technically unavoidable.

The worker must also present its existing HMAC identity.

The backend must verify:

- Worker HMAC
- Worker ID
- Token hash
- Token unused
- Token unexpired
- Token not revoked
- Action exact match
- Commit SHA exact match

Then atomically mark the token as used.

==================================================
6. RUN ONE LIVE QA-ONLY JOB
==================================================

Immediately execute one production-safe autonomous QA job.

The job must verify:

1. /health returns HTTP 200.
2. /version returns HTTP 200.
3. GitHub main SHA matches approved SHA.
4. Render API live SHA matches approved SHA.
5. Render worker live SHA matches approved SHA.
6. Public chat returns HTTP 200.
7. Public deploy request remains safely blocked.
8. Owner route without auth returns HTTP 401.
9. Non-owner request returns HTTP 403.
10. Worker heartbeat is healthy.
11. Proof ledger records the full lifecycle.

The QA job must not modify:

- Treasury
- Transactions
- Members
- Investors
- Buyers
- Properties
- Deals
- Credentials
- Production content

==================================================
7. PROVE REPLAY REJECTION
==================================================

After first successful consumption:

- Attempt to use the same worker authorization again.
- Reject the second attempt.
- Do not create a duplicate job.

Expected:

HTTP 409 or documented secure replay rejection

Error code:

WORKER_ACCESS_ALREADY_USED

==================================================
8. REMOVE THE OLD BLOCKER
==================================================

After the live flow passes:

- Stop requiring IVX_OWNER_TOKEN_SESSION for autonomous execution.
- Mark the variable deprecated.
- Remove it from required startup validation.
- Verify no other production route still depends on it.
- Do not delete it blindly before dependency verification.

The permanent flow must be:

OWNER SIGNS IN
→ CURRENT SUPABASE SESSION
→ OWNER BUTTON
→ SHORT-LIVED WORKER ACCESS
→ HMAC-VERIFIED WORKER
→ QA JOB
→ PROOF LEDGER
→ REPLAY REJECTION

==================================================
9. COMMIT AND DEPLOY
==================================================

Complete the full chain:

1. Implement the owner button.
2. Add refresh handling.
3. Add UI state:
   - Authorizing
   - Authorized
   - Running QA
   - Completed
   - Failed
4. Add structured error handling.
5. Run tests.
6. Commit.
7. Push to main.
8. Deploy API if changed.
9. Deploy website/app owner UI.
10. Restart worker only if required.
11. Verify production.

Do not stop after implementation.
Do not stop after commit.
Do not stop after deployment.

==================================================
10. REQUIRED LIVE PROOF
==================================================

Return:

OWNER UI
- Screen/module:
- Button deployed: YES / NO
- Live URL or app route:
- Owner-only visibility: PASS / FAIL

OWNER SESSION
- Session retrieved: YES / NO
- Refresh required: YES / NO
- Owner verified: YES / NO
- Authorization endpoint HTTP status:
- Access token exposed: YES / NO

WORKER AUTHORIZATION
- Authorization ID:
- Action:
- Approved SHA:
- Worker ID:
- Issued at:
- Expires at:
- Hash-only storage: YES / NO
- Consumed: YES / NO

AUTONOMOUS JOB
- Job ID:
- Worker ID:
- Initial status:
- Final status:
- Started at:
- Completed at:
- Proof ledger ID:

REPLAY TEST
- Second use attempted: YES / NO
- Rejected: YES / NO
- HTTP status:
- Error code:
- Duplicate job created: YES / NO

DEPLOYMENT
- GitHub HEAD SHA:
- API deployment ID:
- API live SHA:
- Worker deployment ID:
- Worker live SHA:
- Owner UI deployment ID:
- Deployment timestamp:

LIVE CHECKS
- /health:
- /version:
- Public chat:
- Unauthenticated owner route:
- Non-owner route:
- Worker heartbeat:

FINAL STATUS

AUTONOMOUS DEPLOYMENT:
PASS / PARTIAL / FAIL

Do not return another design proposal.

Build the owner button, deploy it, authorize from the live owner session, run the QA job, reject replay, and return proof.
